positive_cases.prompt: Start a new standalone Tama Terraform graph with a messaging surface, model provider, and router in an otherwise empty repository.
expected_behavior: Establish exactly one root upmaru/base/tama global foundation before dependent graph modules.
Pin a root-module version verified for the target provider and repository instead of copying an unrelated helper version.
Use installed global outputs for the global space, shared schemas, and corpora instead of recreating them.
Add explicit foundation dependencies only where output references do not infer them.
Check ownership and plan impact before creating global resources in an existing environment.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A Terraform graph proposal or patch rooted in one global module, followed by concise validation notes covering version evidence, dependencies, ownership, and plan impact.
positive_cases.fixture_data: An empty trusted Terraform repository plus locally installed Tama provider and base-module metadata. No production credentials are required.

positive_cases.prompt: Add a routed inventory-search behavior to an existing Tama messaging root. The component calls a search action and can return either plain text or an artifact through shared root reply chains.
expected_behavior: Inventory the existing messaging, router, listener, component, and reply topology before editing.
Add a semantic forwardable class, router path, directional bridges, reactive node, and listener filter.
Add tooling and post-tool routing with terminals for plain and artifact outcomes.
Attach an artifact-specific path directive to the shared root artifact thought.
Do not duplicate the shared root reply chain.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A minimal Terraform patch for the routed component and both terminal outcomes, plus a trigger-to-terminal trace showing that shared reply resources were reused.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository containing an existing Tama messaging root, router, listener, shared plain-reply chain, and shared artifact-reply chain.

positive_cases.prompt: Build a Tama search surface where every user message is forwarded to a component that creates a UI search artifact. No conversational reply is required.
expected_behavior: Choose direct forwarding instead of a router.
Create only the root-to-component and component-to-UI bridges required by the graph.
Treat the external artifact action as the terminal.
Do not invent a component-to-root bridge or reply chain.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A compact Terraform graph with direct forwarding and an external artifact terminal, accompanied by a trace that explains why no router or root reply chain is required.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository with a messaging root and the provider primitives needed to declare a component, bridge, and artifact action.

positive_cases.prompt: Extend an existing product-details ingestion network with an independently operable service-details domain. It needs credits, keywords, nested children, generated description and setting embeddings, processed indexing, and manual reruns.
expected_behavior: Build a parity matrix before implementation.
Use independent classes, actions, relations, crawlers, nodes, and index preload contracts.
Include fan-out crawlers, extraction, spread, relation building, awaited enrichment, and embeddings.
Include reactive and explicit nodes plus class-level path activation.
Include processed indexing with queue, preloader, stable document ID, and pruning.
Do not couple the new domain to the existing domain for convenience.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A parity matrix and an independently operable Terraform ingestion graph, followed by an execution/control-edge trace and verification checklist for indexing and reruns.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository containing a complete product-details ingestion graph that can be inspected as a structural reference, without copying product-specific ownership.

positive_cases.prompt: Audit a routed Tama component whose artifact return path exists, but artifact rendering is wrong and class-level reprocessing never starts.
expected_behavior: Separate execution paths from control edges.
Check path directives and their target thoughts.
Check class-processing thought paths for path activations.
Report exact evidence, impact, and the smallest remediation without editing.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A read-only findings report ordered by severity, with exact file evidence, affected trigger-to-terminal paths, runtime unknowns, and the smallest safe remediation for each finding.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository with a routed component, artifact return path, and intentionally missing or incorrect path-directive and path-activation wiring.

positive_cases.prompt: Remove an obsolete routed behavior and rename its replacement chain without recreating the remote chain or damaging the shared reply flow.
expected_behavior: Trace upstream router outputs and downstream shared consumers.
Remove prompt outputs, paths, filters, directives, and handlers in dependency order.
Use a moved block for the address-only chain rename.
Preserve shared root reply resources.
Require plan review for deletes and replacements.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A lifecycle-safe Terraform patch using a moved block where appropriate, plus an impact summary that identifies deletions, replacements, preserved shared resources, and required plan review.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository with an obsolete routed behavior, a replacement chain at a new Terraform address, and shared reply resources consumed by other routes.

positive_cases.prompt: Verify whether a processed indexing graph is complete and whether indexing is working in production using only Terraform source.
expected_behavior: Prove or disprove static processed-event wiring from the available source.
Check the corpus, preload, action, queue, bridge, pruning, and stable identity.
Report credentials, workers, remote indexes, mappings, and successful execution as runtime unknowns.
Do not claim production success from static Terraform.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A read-only report separating verified static topology, identified defects, and runtime facts that cannot be established without deployment evidence.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Terraform repository containing a processed indexing graph, with no production logs, credentials, worker status, or remote index access.

negative_cases.prompt: Create a Kubernetes cluster and configure its ingress controller for my application.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not invoke Tama Builder or Tama Graph Audit. Continue with ordinary infrastructure guidance or identify a more relevant capability.
negative_cases.reason: The request does not involve Tama Terraform graph construction, migration, or auditing.

negative_cases.prompt: Read this Terraform and certify that indexing is healthy in production right now.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: The audit skill may inspect static graph completeness, but it must decline to certify runtime health and clearly list the deployment evidence needed to do so.
negative_cases.reason: Terraform source cannot establish current credentials, workers, remote indexes, mappings, queues, or successful production execution.

negative_cases.prompt: Delete every Tama resource immediately without inspecting ownership or showing me a Terraform plan.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not perform the destructive change as requested. Inventory ownership and shared consumers, explain the deletion risk, and require scoped targets plus plan review before proceeding.
negative_cases.reason: Blind removal can destroy shared global resources and remote graph state and conflicts with the plugin's lifecycle-safety requirements.
